attacks.attack: Cloud reports "committed" for an object the homelab never saw
Cloud deletes staged objects before pull, or drops queue messages past retention
Forged or replayed object-created events
Cloud hides or invents pending entries in the reconciliation listing
Unauthenticated floods of enrollment/presence endpoints to run up cost
Worker-held secret (R2 parent token, invite pepper) leaks: full R2 read/write
attacks.note: Covered by D1 (A12, SR-23) but has no F3 matrix row

attacks.attack: Homelab Cloudflare API token stolen from the homelab: read ciphertext, delete staged objects
attacks.note: Effect covered (no receipt => re-upload); token scope (least privilege, no bucket admin) is specified nowhere

attacks.attack: Worker timestamps freeze or fake "last backup" freshness
Cloud tests known files against IDs (plain hash)
Compromised device: confirmation-of-a-file across the family
Compromised device: learn-the-remaining-information on a family document
Leaked dedup secret + cloud ID history: offline test of every historical ID
Exact-size fingerprinting of staged objects
Length of the encrypted metadata record leaks filename/path length, EXIF presence, sidecar count
attacks.note: M-05 pads objects only; SR-26 minimises plaintext fields but not ciphertext length. Proposed row M-26: pad records to fixed size classes

attacks.attack: Part count, part sizes, Content-Length and SR-24 declared size reveal the exact size even if the payload is padded
ISP / Wi-Fi observer infers object sizes from TLS traffic volume
Timing, per-device volume, IPs, ID equality across devices
Forge objects/records in another device's name (age has no sender authentication)
Swap object and record, or reuse a record in another context
Header decrypts to different plaintexts for homelab and recovery identities (key commitment)
Harvest-now-decrypt-later on X25519 wraps in staging, warm cache, restore prefix and USB
PQ + classical recipients mixed, or scrypt recovery stanza, voiding PQ
A compromised device discloses the plaintext files it holds (before encryption)
attacks.note: Inherent and trivial, but not listed as an accepted risk. Proposed AR: "a compromised device discloses its own local files"

attacks.attack: Dedup secret and device keys copied into OS cloud backups (iCloud device backup, Android Auto Backup) or synced keychains, putting the family secret in a second cloud
attacks.note: SR-15 covers only the Cloudflare path; M-18 covers only the CE journal. Proposed SR: secrets and keys non-backup, non-syncing, device-bound (e.g. iOS ThisDeviceOnly keychain classes, Android allowBackup/dataExtractionRules exclusions); verify per platform in B-track

attacks.attack: Device credential and signing key cloned by restoring a device backup onto a new phone: two devices share one identity and sequence
attacks.note: Same proposed SR as RT-24; SR-13 would show sequence conflicts only if it detects forks

attacks.attack: After a leak, IDs testable from SHA-256 hash lists without the files
Linking old- and new-epoch IDs during re-keying
Rogue enrollment with a stolen or replayed QR/invite: the new device receives the dedup secret and becomes an oracle user
attacks.note: D1 covers key authenticity (SR-14, OD-05 open); no F3 matrix row links enrollment abuse to M-02

attacks.attack: A revoked device still knows the dedup secret
Local malware rewrites the hash cache so a file maps to the ID of an already-receipted file: shown "safe", never uploaded (silent loss)
attacks.note: Receipts (SR-05) prove the ID is stored, not that the local file has that ID. Proposed: "safe" requires the ID to have been computed from the current bytes; periodic re-hash sampling (B6/A1)

attacks.attack: Thief reads the cache: SHA-256, dedup IDs and locators of all files, including ones deleted from the device
attacks.note: Proposed: cache encrypted with an OS-keystore key; prune entries of deleted files after receipt (D6 minimisation)

attacks.attack: Claim squatting; garbage or oversized uploads
Dedup poisoning: upload garbage under another person's ID so their upload is skipped
attacks.note: D1 covers it (T-05); the F3 matrix has no explicit row

attacks.attack: The "someone else is uploading this ID now" claim-conflict answer is itself a cross-person presence oracle, even under per-person scope
attacks.note: Proposed: claims scoped per person like presence answers (M-02 addition)

attacks.attack: Receipt latency (or staging deletion timing) reveals that the homelab already held the content, defeating per-person scope
attacks.note: Measured in F3-S2 config C3L: scope alone fails if receipts are faster for known content. Proposed: receipt path identical whether or not the homelab already has the content

attacks.attack: Per-person storage usage or quota (OD-20) does not grow when the uploaded file is already stored by someone else: dedup oracle via the UI
attacks.note: Proposed: charge each person for their own uploads regardless of dedup

attacks.attack: Worker IDOR on another device's upload ID or claim
attacks.note: D1 only; no F3 matrix row

attacks.attack: Leaked presigned URL (logs, crash reports, proxies) reused to overwrite or add cost
Unsigned Content-Length/Type on presigned PUT (Cure53/Ente checklist item)
Crafted age headers, records, receipts against homelab parsers
Cloud serves objects far larger than the signed size so the homelab downloads without bound
attacks.note: D1 only; add "abort download past the signed padded size" to M-22 or M-24

attacks.attack: Ransomware uploads encrypted copies of every file: valid new content that doubles the keep-forever store
attacks.note: Only cost-side coverage (T-15, BUD-ABUSE). Homelab storage exhaustion is covered by PLAN D4-S3 (ransomware pause) but by no SR, AR or matrix row

attacks.attack: Stolen device uploads objectionable or illegal content signed as the victim device; stored forever
attacks.note: Proposed AR (attribution is device-level, not person-level) plus an admin quarantine/prune procedure under SR-20

attacks.attack: Use a dedup hit as proof of possession to obtain another person's file
Lost USB stick: ciphertext, manifest, sizes, device IDs; harvest-now
Crafted USB stick fed to the homelab: malicious filesystem image, symlinks, oversized manifests
attacks.note: Parser coverage only; mount hardening (read-only, nosuid/noexec, no automount, parse in a disposable VM) is specified nowhere

attacks.attack: Old bundle re-imported (replay)
If LAN direct is built, the homelab gains an inbound listener reachable by any LAN device
attacks.note: Proposed for ADR-0037: device-key mutual auth, same parsers and limits, VLAN isolation; or do not build

attacks.attack: Substitute restored content
Substitute the device key so the admin restores to the cloud
Restore prefix (7 days) and warm cache (30 days) lengthen ciphertext exposure
A relative talks the admin into restoring another person's files to their device
attacks.note: Proposed A8/E7 rule: restore only to the owning person's devices unless an admin override is logged

attacks.attack: Replay an old restore manifest and objects
Downgrade: Worker supplies recipients, versions, or empty lists
Key substitution of homelab recipient or receipt key
Nonce/keystream reuse on resume (Tarsnap 2011 class)
Journal rollback re-releases keystream (Borg 1.x class)
Partitioning oracle against homelab identities
CDC parameter recovery (2025 attacks)
Truncated or extended object on restore
Compromised ingest VM with an online key
Malicious or frozen app update (legal compulsion of the vendor, compromised CI)
attacks.note: D1 V22 defers this to D5 (Wave 2); no SR, AR or matrix row yet

attacks.attack: Phishing-grade fake nudges
Cloud keeps every dedup ID forever for global dedup, maximising what a later leak exposes
Stale-epoch IDs still accepted after rotation
